svg.title: The scalar coupling refinement has a direct compactness proof. For each level m the represented action supplies the interval bound bβm/2 ≤βN,p,m ≤2 bβm whenever m ≤N. Extend βN,p,m to N < m by the value bβm, solely for this compactness argument. Regard the extended array at N as a point of the countable product Q p,m[ bβm/2, 2 bβm]. This product is compact metrizable. Extract one mesh subsequence along which every coordinate (p,m) converges to ap,m. Then regard (ap(k),m)m along the requested volume sequence as points of Q m[ bβm/2, 2 bβm], and extract one volume subsequence along which they converge to Bm for every m. For fixed m, the auxiliary extension agrees eventually with the original coupling because the mesh index tends to infinity. Thus the chosen refinement has the stated iterated limit for every level. Any later mesh and volume refinements preserve it. These limiting coefficients retain the running slope. Write
